# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 47 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 47 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_047_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 4 — The Devil Is Afraid of Faithful People

**47:1** I asked him again: can people who live in the ordinary world actually keep these commandments? He said: "Yes, they can. I gave these commandments specifically to people like you who live in the world. Here's what I'm telling you: if you keep them without adding worldly desires to them, you will live. But if you mix even a little worldly craving into them, you won't be able to keep them."

**47:2** He continued: "Let me also tell you about the devil's methods — because he works too. When a righteous person comes near, the devil gets scared. But when a double-minded, weak-willed person comes near, the devil isn't scared at all — he immediately enters that person."

**47:3** "A faith-filled person stands firm against the devil and doesn't fear him, because the Lord is with him and God's power is in him. But a double-minded person is afraid of the devil and easily falls under his influence. The devil gets into that person and does whatever he wants with them."

**47:4** "Now, the Lord himself is the Angel of Righteousness. He strengthens everyone who has faith and does good. Trust him, and you will conquer the devil — because the devil has absolutely no power over you. Just believe in God and trust him. The Lord will come and drive the devil away from you and strip him of his power over you."

**47:5** "The only people the devil has access to are the double-minded — the ones who waver, who fear him, who have let go of their faith. He comes back to them, moves in, and does every kind of evil through them. But he can't stand against people who have genuine faith in their hearts. So this is the power of the commandment: whoever believes in God and does good will have tremendous joy."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the confident spiritual warfare tone of Mandate 12.*
